P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer of Gaunt Street, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and old friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. Enfield showed him a sinister door and told of a man who trampled a child. Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, who had never heard of Hyde. Utterson kept watch by the by-street door until he accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He then learned from Poole that Jekyll was out and that Hyde had a key. He now fears Jekyll is in deep waters.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P11.name: the maid servant
P11.intro: witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.

P12.name: Sir Danvers Carew

$set: an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair

P12.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

P13.name: Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard
P13.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

P15.tagline: employer of the maid who saw Hyde

P16.name: Mr. Guest
P16.intro: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
P16.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
P16.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

P1.name: 阿Q
P1.intro: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P2.name: 我
P2.intro: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

P3.name: 赵太爷
P3.intro: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

P5.name: 赵太爷的儿子茂才先生

$set: 赵太爷的儿子茂才先生

P5.intro: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
P5.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
P5.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

P12.name: 闲人
P12.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

P14.name: 王胡
P14.intro: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
P14.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
P14.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

P16.name: 小尼姑
P16.intro: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

P18.name: 吴妈
P18.intro: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
P18.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
P18.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

P25.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

P2.name: 我
P2.intro: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

P3.name: 赵太爷
P3.intro: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

P5.name: 赵太爷的儿子茂才先生

$set: 赵太爷的儿子茂才先生

P5.intro: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
P5.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
P5.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

P12.name: 闲人
P12.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

P14.name: 王胡
P14.intro: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
P14.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
P14.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

P15.name: 钱太爷的大儿子
P15.intro: 进过洋学堂、到过东洋，有假辫子，打阿Q
P15.tagline: 进过洋学堂、到过东洋，有假辫子，打阿Q

P16.name: 小尼姑
P16.intro: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

P17.name: 酒店里的人
P17.intro: 围观并笑赏阿Q欺侮小尼姑的众人
P17.tagline: 围观并笑赏阿Q欺侮小尼姑的众人

P18.name: 吴妈
P18.intro: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
P18.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
P18.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

P25.name: 小D
P25.intro: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
P25.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
P25.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town, acquainted with Dr. Jekyll. He dislikes asking questions and calls this delicacy. He once collared a man who walked over a child and forced him to pay a hundred pounds, then spent the night in his chambers and proved the cheque genuine at the bank. He named the man as Hyde and described him as deformed and detestable. He later learned the sinister door was a back way to Jekyll's house. On a Sunday walk with Utterson he said the Hyde story was at an end, and after seeing Jekyll at the window he left the court in silence, pale with horror.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, owner of the house with laboratory and cabinet, and the friend and client of Mr. Utterson. He is tall and well built, known for charities and religion, but has become fanciful and estranged from Dr. Lanyon. His will left all his possessions to Edward Hyde, and he admitted Hyde dictated its terms. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, then resumed his old friendships before shutting his door against Utterson and vowing extreme seclusion. He was last seen sitting sadly at the middle window, declining to walk out. He is said to have been made away with eight days ago, and his body has not been found.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly butler of Dr. Jekyll's house and the servant who directs the search after the cabinet is broken open. He is frightened and worn, with a white face and a harsh broken voice, and for about a week he has been unable to bear the situation. He long served Jekyll, admitted Utterson to the cabinet, and reported that Jekyll confined himself over the laboratory. When he came to Utterson's house at night, he said the doctor had shut himself in and he feared foul play. He led Utterson to the laboratory, told of the masked figure, and struck the door with an axe. He now hands Utterson the sealed packet and awaits the police.

P11.name: the maid servant
P11.intro: witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.

P12.name: Sir Danvers Carew

$set: an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair

P12.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

P13.name: Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard
P13.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

P15.name: the master of the servant maid

P15.intro: employer of the maid who saw Hyde
P15.tagline: employer of the maid who saw Hyde

P16.name: Mr. Guest
P16.intro: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
P16.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
P16.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

P17.name: the housemaid
P17.intro: servant who weeps hysterically
P17.tagline: Servant who weeps hysterically
P17.bio: The housemaid is a servant in Dr. Jekyll's house, subordinate to Poole and a colleague of the cook. She is hysterical and weeping. When Poole led Utterson into the hall, all the servants were huddled in fear, and she whimpered while the maid wept loudly. She remains in the hall with the other frightened servants as Utterson and Poole proceed to the laboratory. Her present situation is one of terror and grief among the household while the search for Jekyll continues.

P18.tagline: servant who greets Utterson

P20.name: the voice
P20.intro: voice inside the cabinet refusing entry
P20.tagline: Voice inside the cabinet refusing entry
P20.bio: The voice is the unseen speaker inside Dr. Jekyll's cabinet, heard by Poole and Mr. Utterson during the night search. It complains that it cannot see anyone and begs Utterson for mercy. It is connected to Poole only as the servant who knocks and calls through the door. After Poole reports that the doctor has shut himself in, the voice answers from within and refuses entry. Utterson recognizes it as Hyde's voice and orders the door down. The voice is now silent, its speaker found dead inside the cabinet.

P1.name: 阿Q
P1.intro: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

P16.intro: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town, acquainted with Dr. Jekyll. He dislikes asking questions and calls this delicacy. He once collared a man who walked over a child and forced him to pay a hundred pounds, then spent the night in his chambers and proved the cheque genuine at the bank. He named the man as Hyde and described him as deformed and detestable. He later learned the sinister door was a back way to Jekyll's house. On a Sunday walk with Utterson he said the Hyde story was at an end, and after seeing Jekyll at the window he left the court in silence, pale with horror.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir.
P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, colleague of Dr. Lanyon, and lawyer Utterson's acquaintance, known for charities and religion. He is hunted across the land as Carew's murderer. He swore never to set eyes on Hyde again, admitted Hyde dictated his will, and after Hyde vanished resumed his old friendships. He then shut his door against Utterson, vowed extreme seclusion, and spoke of an unnameable punishment. On the ninth of January he begged Lanyon to force open his cabinet, take the fourth drawer, and receive a midnight messenger. Lanyon obeyed, and Jekyll confessed his moral turpitude with tears.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor.
P8.bio: Hastie Lanyon is a doctor and colleague of Henry Jekyll, and an old friend of Mr. Utterson. He is cautious and suspicious of Jekyll's sanity. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind, and later refused to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him. After dining with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, he was shocked by his own decayed appearance and declared himself a doomed man who would never recover. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened his sealed envelope.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house.
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, obeyed by the housemaid, cook, and knife-boy, and directed by Mr. Utterson in the search. He is afraid and cannot bear it, with a white face and harsh broken voice. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, that Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, and that all servants had orders to obey Hyde. Later he reported Jekyll confined and silent, came to Utterson at night, and said he thought there had been foul play. He and Utterson broke in and found Hyde's body. He currently awaits Lanyon's arrival with a locksmith.

P11.name: the maid servant
P11.intro: witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.

P12.name: Sir Danvers Carew

$set: an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair

P12.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

P13.name: Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard
P13.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

P16.intro: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
P16.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
P16.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

P17.name: the housemaid
P17.intro: servant who weeps hysterically
P17.tagline: Servant who weeps hysterically
P17.bio: The housemaid is a servant in Dr. Jekyll's house, subordinate to Poole and a colleague of the cook. She is hysterical and weeping. When Poole led Utterson into the hall, all the servants were huddled in fear, and she whimpered while the maid wept loudly. She remains in the hall with the other frightened servants as Utterson and Poole proceed to the laboratory. Her present situation is one of terror and grief among the household while the search for Jekyll continues.

P20.bio: The voice is the unseen speaker inside Dr. Jekyll's cabinet, heard by Poole and Mr. Utterson during the night search. It complains that it cannot see anyone and begs Utterson for mercy. It is connected to Poole only as the servant who knocks and calls through the door. After Poole reports that the doctor has shut himself in, the voice answers from within and refuses entry. Utterson recognizes it as Hyde's voice and orders the door down. The voice is now silent, its speaker found dead inside the cabinet.

At midnight he knocked gently and crouched against the portico pillars; when Lanyon asked if he came from Dr. Jekyll, he gestured yes. He glanced back at a policeman and hurried inside. Lanyon then saw him clearly for the first time and was struck by his appearance. He is currently at Lanyon's house, having come secretly at midnight in Jekyll's name.

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer of Gaunt Street, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and old friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. Enfield showed him a sinister door and told of a man who trampled a child. Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, who had never heard of Hyde. Utterson kept watch by the by-street door until he accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He then learned from Poole that Jekyll was out and that Hyde had a key. He now fears Jekyll is in deep waters.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P11.name: the maid servant
P11.intro: witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.

P12.name: Sir Danvers Carew

$set: an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair

P12.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

P13.name: Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard
P13.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

P1.name: 阿Q
P1.intro: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P2.name: 我
P2.intro: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

P3.name: 赵太爷
P3.intro: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P11.name: the maid servant
P11.intro: witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.

P12.name: Sir Danvers Carew

$set: an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair

P12.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

P13.name: Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard
P13.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

P16.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

P1.name: 阿Q
P1.intro: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P2.name: 我
P2.intro: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

P3.name: 赵太爷
P3.intro: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

P16.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

P16.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P11.name: the maid servant
P11.intro: witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.

P12.name: Sir Danvers Carew

$set: an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair

P12.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

P13.name: Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard
P13.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer of Gaunt Street, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and old friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. Enfield showed him a sinister door and told of a man who trampled a child. Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, who had never heard of Hyde. Utterson kept watch by the by-street door until he accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He then learned from Poole that Jekyll was out and that Hyde had a key. He now fears Jekyll is in deep waters.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

P7.name: Dr. Jekyll
P7.intro: doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

P8.name: Dr. Lanyon
P8.intro: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
P8.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

P10.name: Poole
P10.intro: elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P2.name: 我
P2.intro: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者

P3.name: 赵太爷

He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. P1.name: 阿Q
P1.intro: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P2.name: 我
P2.intro: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

P3.name: 赵太爷
P3.intro: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

On a Sunday walk with Enfield, he was shown a sinister door and heard Enfield's account of a man who trampled a girl and paid with a cheque. Utterson asked whether the cheque drawer lived there, asked the man's name, and asked whether Hyde used a key. He said he already knew the other party's name. P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town

On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: The man in the middle, later named Hyde, is a person of extraordinary appearance who gives a feeling of deformity. He is cool, sneering, and Satan-like. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, then was collared by Enfield and brought back to the group around the child. The doctor turned sick and white with desire to kill him. Threatened with scandal, he was forced to pay a hundred pounds. He led them to the door, unlocked it, and returned with gold and a cheque, offering to stay until the banks opened and cash it himself. They spent the night in Enfield's chambers and went to the bank next day. He still has a key and used it a week ago.

P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor

He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

P10.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house

He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. P1.name: 阿Q
P1.intro: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
P1.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

P2.name: 我
P2.intro: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
P2.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

P3.name: 赵太爷
P3.intro: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

P16.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P2.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

P3.name: 赵太爷
P3.intro: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
P3.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

P4.name: 地保
P4.intro: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
P4.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

P12.name: 闲人
P12.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

P14.name: 王胡
P14.intro: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
P14.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
P14.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

P16.name: 小尼姑
P16.intro: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
P16.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

P18.name: 吴妈
P18.intro: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
P18.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
P18.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

P25.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
P25.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

P1.name: Mr. Utterson
P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

P2.name: Mr. Richard Enfield
P2.intro: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
P2.bio: Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town, acquainted with Dr. Jekyll. He dislikes asking questions and calls this delicacy. He once collared a man who walked over a child and forced him to pay a hundred pounds, then spent the night in his chambers and proved the cheque genuine at the bank. He named the man as Hyde and described him as deformed and detestable. He later learned the sinister door was a back way to Jekyll's house. On a Sunday walk with Utterson he said the Hyde story was at an end, and after seeing Jekyll at the window he left the court in silence, pale with horror.

P3.name: the man in the middle
P3.intro: tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

P4.tagline: child knocked down by the man
